newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra guarantees lower airport landing fee.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra guarantees lower airport landing fee.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Wednesday he could guarantee lower landing charges at privatised airports, which would maintain downward pressure on airfares.
"Landing charges at privatised airports are guaranteed to fall significantly in real terms, keeping downward pressure on airfares," Sharp said in a statement.

Sharp announced on Wednesday the so-called "X-factors" for the CPI (consumer price index)-minus-X pricing formula that the government will use to ensure landing charges remain capped for the first five years after airport privatisation.
He said Melbourne airport would have an X-factor of 4.0 percent, while the X-factors for Brisbane and Perth airports would be set at 4.5 percent and 5.5 percent respectively.

Melbourne, Perth and Brisbane airports are the first to be sold as part of the government's airport privatisation programme. There are currently 10 consortiums short-listed for bids for the sale of 50 year leases for the airports.

"These generous X values mean airlines can be assured that landing charges at privatised airports will follow a downward trend over the first five years following privatisation," Sharp said. "This restraint should also help keep airfares down."
He said the X-factors were set after consultation with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), which would administer the price cap arrangements for five year period.
The X-factors reflected the significant productivity improvements and growth that the government expected new airport operators to achieve in the first five years of their leases.

"Over time, the government wants to see airport operators and their customers negotiating directly on pricing and investment decisions, but with the ACCC remaining empowered to prevent monopoly pricing," he said.
Sharp also released the government's pricing policy paper detailing the pricing regime which would apply to privatised airports.
